name: Dan Hawkins
bio:
Dan works for government and law enforcement on the implications of future tech for public safety. His work informs policy, operations, and strategy,

Key areas: Foresight | Clarifying complexity | Grounding innovation | Malicious uses of AI | Disinformation | Deepfakes | Online trust & safety.

name: Jessica Figueras
bio:
Jessica works at the intersection of tech, government and civil society in the fields of cyber security and trust, online safety, risk, regulation, and social impact.

Key areas: Strategy and leadership | Growth, market development and innovation | Cybersecurity | Data/AI and digital transformation | board perspective, risk and governance | Government, politics & policy | Regulated industries.

name: Broderick McDonald
bio:
Broderick is Director of the Oxford Disinformation & Extremism Lab, a CETaS fellow at the Turing Institute, and a Research Fellow at KCL's XCEPT Research Programme among other roles.

Key areas: AI security | Online harms | Hybrid warfare | Disinformation | Terrorism | Fraud | Geopolitical risk | Counterintelligence | OSINT.

name: Paul Ridgewell
bio:
Paul is an experienced expert analyst, and author of AI Crime Insights, a monthly horizon-scanning newsletter covering AI-enabled crime and law enforcement responses.

Key areas: Research | Foresight | Artificial intelligence | Cybersecurity & cybercrime | Emerging technology | Internet architecture | Data-enabled law enforcement | Communications technology | Financial services technology.

name: Windsor Holden
bio:
Windsor has over 27 years’ experience as a technology consultant and analyst, specialising in actionable insight for government and enterprise.

Key areas: Emerging Technologies | Digital ID | AI Security | Telecom Resilience | Payments | Drones | Internet of Space | Hazard detection.
